textbookText: 9.4: Nitrogen Nitrogen Daniel Rutherford (3 November 1749 – 15 November 1819) was a Scottish physician, chemist and botanist who is known for the isolation of nitrogen in 1772. He postulated the existence of nitrogen gas that does not catalyze the combustion reaction. This inability of nitrogen was tested by conducting an experiment where oxygen and carbon dioxide were eliminated by burning the atmospheric oxygen leaving behind the gas called nitrogen.
Element: Nitrogen Symbol: N Atomic Number: 7 Atomic Weight: 14.007 amu Molecular Formula: N2
Electronic configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p3 Group: 15 Period: 3rd Block: p block element Valency: 3
Nitrogen is a non-metallic element. It is a colourless, odourless and tasteless gas. The Earth's atmosphere consists of 75.5% nitrogen by weight and 78% nitrogen by volume.
